title: episodic-workload-simulator-to-improve-pr-performance-gating
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Current PR gating relies on single-point throughput snapshots and p95 samples that miss short-lived burst regressions (e.g., cold-KV-cache spikes, streaming context fallout). Consequence: regressions that only appear under episodic/bursty traffic slip into main and surface in production as customer-facing latency spikes and higher per-token costs.

Goal: Build an 'Episodic Workload Simulator' harness for CI that synthesizes short, realistic workload episodes (bursty requests, long-context streaming, cache-warmup patterns) and produces a composite performance score used by PR gates. The harness should: 1) measure steady-state tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) across episodes, 2) model expected baseline using a Bayesian rolling baseline that is robust to seasonal shifts, 3) flag regressions with an ensemble decision rule combining delta on tokens/sec and an asymmetric penalty for p95 regressions, 4) be cheap enough to run on PRs (sampled fast-run episodes) and to run nightly for baselines.

Scope: Implementation includes workload generator service, CI job templates, metric collectors, baseline updater, gating rule integration with sentinel, and dashboards for investigation. Out of scope: upstream kernel optimizations — those are separate follow-ups once a regression is triaged.

Success criteria: (a) CI detects 90%+ of synthetic injected regressions in staging at or above our target SLO delta; (b) reduced production regressions tied to episodic patterns by 40% in the next quarter; (c) <20% CI cost increase via sampling and adaptive episode lengths.
comments: 2026-01-12 - Aisha Raman: Initial proposal drafted after incident analysis (prod spikes on 2025-12-10). Added scope and success criteria. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Episodic+Workload+Simulator

2026-01-20 - Jonah Li: Spike complete. Implemented first synthetic episode runner that replays a distribution of request lengths derived from customer telemetry. Proof-of-concept measures tokens/sec and p95 in a single VM. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/244
2026-01-28 - PM feedback (Priya Menon): Ask to include an ensemble decision rule and a conservative fail-open policy for low-sample PR runs. Added to scope.

2026-02-03 - Design review (Elena Torres): Dashboard wireframes reviewed. Agreed on composite score visualization and time-aligned waterfall for KV-warmup. Action: design to provide SVGs for console panel by 2026-02-10.

2026-02-12 - Jonah Li: Implemented Bayesian baseline updater (lightweight conjugate priors over log-throughput). Baseline stored as rolling window with changepoint detection. Nightly job created: perf-nightly/episodic-baselines. Artifact: gs://redwood-perf/episodic/2026-02-12-baseline.json

2026-02-22 - QA (Marta Kovac): Ran ~50 synthetic-injection experiments against the harness. Detection rate for +-10% throughput regressions: 92% when episodes include KV cold-starts; for pure steady-state regressions detection is consistent with existing gates. Found noise during very long-context episodes; suggested trimming max-sequence to 5k for PR runs.

2026-03-01 - Jonah Li: Implemented PR sampling strategy: short episodes (20 sec) seeded from customer clusters and one longer episode (90 sec) for nightly. Added asymmetric scoring: p95 degradation >5% weights 2x relative to tokens/sec drop. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/267

2026-03-05 - PM (Priya Menon): Requested an opt-in threshold override for experimental repos. Also requested a telemetry tag to correlate CI failures with customer incidents. Added labels and dependency notes.
implementation_notes: Architecture: workload-generator (go) -> run orchestrator (k8s Job) -> metric-exporter (Prometheus counter + histograms) -> baseline service (Python lambda) -> gating adapter (sentinel webhook). CI: small GPU pool with pre-warmed cache images. Trade-offs considered: full replay vs synthetic sampling (chose sampling to reduce cost), Bayesian baseline vs simple moving average (Bayesian chosen for robustness to infrequent but large shifts).
next_steps: 1) Merge PR #267 and enable feature-flagged PR runs for core/runtime repo. 2) Add opt-in override for experimental repos and telemetry tag. 3) Run 2-week shadow runs on main branch and compare nightly baselines. 4) Iterate on episode parameters per QA feedback (trim long-context PR episode).
investigation_summary: Root cause that motivated this ticket: production incidents where cold KV-cache on rare customer flows caused p95 bursts without changing average tokens/sec. Existing gates missed these because sampling lacked episodic patterns. The episodic harness reproduces this behavior and surfaces regressions earlier.
notes_for_oncall: If a PR gates on episodic-harness failure, triage should: pull failed run artifact from gs://redwood-perf/episodic/{run-id}, examine waterfall KV-warmup trace on Grafana, and if it is a model/kernel regression, tag @runtime-team. If noise suspected, re-run with longer episode or switch to nightly baseline to validate.
